name: Missed Contacts
description: Routing attempts where the system offered a conversation to an agent but no successful acceptance occurred. NOT the same as abandonment (customer left before agent).
search_text: Missed contacts routing attempt no_ready_agents no_shift_coverage no agent pickup week over week
disambiguation: Use RoutingAttempt.outcome for routing-side misses. Use Conversation.end_reason + assigned_at IS NULL for customer-side abandonment.
business_rules: Missed contact = RoutingAttempt.outcome IN ['no_ready_agents', 'no_shift_coverage'] (no agent available to accept)
Filter by created_at date range using datetime($period_start) / datetime($period_end) — properties are Neo4j ZONED DATETIME (UTC)
For 'why increase/decrease': use diagnostic_template in ONE query — returns queue, current, previous, delta
If previous=0 but current>0, note partial history — data may not cover full comparison window
Contact node key is cdp_id; Conversation key is id
cypher_template: MATCH (c:Conversation)-[:HAS_ROUTING_ATTEMPT]->(ra:RoutingAttempt) WHERE ra.created_at >= datetime($period_start) AND ra.created_at < datetime($period_end) AND ra.outcome IN ['no_ready_agents', 'no_shift_coverage'] RETURN count(ra) AS missed_count
diagnostic_template: MATCH (c:Conversation)-[:HAS_ROUTING_ATTEMPT]->(ra:RoutingAttempt)-[:TARGETED_QUEUE]->(q:Queue) WHERE ra.outcome IN ['no_ready_agents','no_shift_coverage'] WITH q.name AS dimension, sum(CASE WHEN ra.created_at >= datetime($period_start) AND ra.created_at < datetime($period_end) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS current, sum(CASE WHEN ra.created_at >= datetime($compare_start) AND ra.created_at < datetime($compare_end) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS previous RETURN dimension, current, previous, current - previous AS delta ORDER BY abs(current - previous) DESC LIMIT 5
examples: Why did missed contacts increase this week?
Which queue has the most missed contacts?

name: Abandonment Rate
description: Percentage of conversations where the customer disconnected before being handled by an agent.
search_text: Abandonment rate customer disconnect before agent conversation
disambiguation: Different from Missed Contacts which measures routing-side failures after offer.
business_rules: Abandoned = Conversation ended without agent assignment OR end_reason indicates customer disconnect
Numerator: conversations with assigned_at IS NULL or end_reason in customer-abandon codes
cypher_template: MATCH (c:Conversation) WHERE c.created_at >= datetime($period_start) AND c.created_at < datetime($period_end) WITH count(c) AS total, sum(CASE WHEN c.assigned_at IS NULL AND c.ended_at IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS abandoned RETURN abandoned, total, toFloat(abandoned)/total AS abandonment_rate

name: SLA Breach Rate

cypher_template: MATCH (c:Conversation)-[:HAS_SLA]->(si:SLAInstance) WHERE si.breached_at >= datetime($period_start) AND si.breached_at < datetime($period_end) RETURN count(si) AS breach_count

name: First Contact Resolution (FCR)

name: Average Handle Time (AHT)
description: Average duration from agent assignment to resolution.
search_text: Average handle time AHT assigned_at resolved_at duration
business_rules: Only include conversations where both timestamps exist
cypher_template: MATCH (c:Conversation) WHERE c.assigned_at IS NOT NULL AND c.resolved_at IS NOT NULL AND c.resolved_at >= datetime($period_start) RETURN avg(duration.between(c.assigned_at, c.resolved_at).seconds) AS aht_seconds

name: Service Level
description: Percentage of conversations where first agent response occurred within SLA threshold.
search_text: Service level percentage answered within threshold first response
business_rules: Or compare first_agent_response_at - queued_at against threshold seconds
cypher_template: MATCH (c:Conversation)-[:HAS_SLA]->(si:SLAInstance) WHERE c.created_at >= datetime($period_start) AND c.first_agent_response_at IS NOT NULL WITH count(c) AS total, sum(CASE WHEN c.first_agent_response_at <= si.first_response_due_at THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS met RETURN toFloat(met)/total AS service_level

name: Queue Wait Time
description: Time from entering queue to agent assignment.
search_text: Queue wait time queued_at assigned_at IN_QUEUE
cypher_template: MATCH (c:Conversation)-[:IN_QUEUE]->(q:Queue) WHERE c.queued_at IS NOT NULL AND c.assigned_at IS NOT NULL AND c.created_at >= datetime($period_start) RETURN q.name AS queue, avg(duration.between(c.queued_at, c.assigned_at).seconds) AS avg_wait_seconds ORDER BY avg_wait_seconds DESC LIMIT 10

name: Transfer Rate
description: Conversations that were transferred to another queue or agent.
search_text: Transfer rate HAS_TRANSFER TRANSFERRED_TO escalation
cypher_template: MATCH (c:Conversation)-[:HAS_TRANSFER]->(t:Transfer) WHERE t.requested_at >= datetime($period_start) AND t.requested_at < datetime($period_end) RETURN count(DISTINCT c) AS transfer_count

name: Conversation Volume
description: Total count of conversations in a time period, breakdown by channel or queue.
search_text: Conversation volume count by channel queue period
business_rules: Group by channel property or THROUGH relationship
cypher_template: MATCH (c:Conversation)-[:THROUGH]->(ch:Channel) WHERE c.created_at >= datetime($period_start) AND c.created_at < datetime($period_end) RETURN ch.name AS channel, count(c) AS volume ORDER BY volume DESC

name: Customer
description: A Contact who has at least one valid Order or SalesOrder.
search_text: Customer contact with order purchase PLACED PLACED_BY
business_rules: Order/SalesOrder must have completed or paid status
cypher_template: MATCH (ct:Contact)-[:PLACED]->(o:Order) WHERE o.status IN ['completed', 'paid'] RETURN count(DISTINCT ct) AS customer_count
examples: How many customers do we have?

name: Lead
description: A Contact with CRM overlay showing lead status but not yet converted to Deal.
search_text: Lead prospect ContactProfile OVERLAY_OF lead_status
business_rules: Lead when lead_status set and CONVERTED_TO Deal absent
cypher_template: MATCH (cp:ContactProfile)-[:OVERLAY_OF]->(ct:Contact) WHERE cp.lead_status IS NOT NULL AND NOT (cp)-[:CONVERTED_TO]->(:Deal) RETURN count(DISTINCT ct) AS lead_count

name: Churn Risk
description: Contacts with elevated churn_score on CustomerScore node.
search_text: Churn risk CustomerScore HAS_SCORES churn_score retention
cypher_template: MATCH (ct:Contact)-[:HAS_SCORES]->(cs:CustomerScore) WHERE cs.churn_score >= $threshold RETURN ct.cdp_id, ct.first_name, ct.last_name, cs.churn_score ORDER BY cs.churn_score DESC LIMIT 20

name: Customer Lifetime Value (CLV)
description: Total revenue from a contact across all orders.
search_text: Customer lifetime value CLV order total_amount PLACED
cypher_template: MATCH (ct:Contact)-[:PLACED]->(o:Order) RETURN ct.cdp_id, sum(o.total_amount) AS clv ORDER BY clv DESC LIMIT 20

name: Segment Membership
description: Contacts belonging to a marketing or analytics segment.
search_text: Segment membership BELONGS_TO_SEGMENT contact count
business_rules: Segment defined by Tenant via DEFINES_SEGMENT
cypher_template: MATCH (ct:Contact)-[:BELONGS_TO_SEGMENT]->(s:Segment) RETURN s.segment_name AS segment, count(ct) AS members ORDER BY members DESC
examples: How many contacts in VIP segment?

name: Deal Pipeline
description: Sales deals tracked by stage with amount and expected close date.
search_text: Deal pipeline stage amount WITH_COMPANY PRIMARY_CONTACT win rate
cypher_template: MATCH (d:Deal) WHERE d.closed_at IS NULL RETURN d.stage AS stage, count(d) AS deals, sum(d.amount) AS pipeline_value ORDER BY pipeline_value DESC
diagnostic_template: MATCH (d:Deal) WITH d.stage AS dimension, sum(CASE WHEN d.updated_at >= datetime($period_start) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS current, sum(CASE WHEN d.updated_at >= datetime($compare_start) AND d.updated_at < datetime($compare_end) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS previous RETURN dimension, current, previous, current - previous AS delta ORDER BY abs(delta) DESC LIMIT 5

name: Account
description: Maps to Company node — organizational entity grouping contacts, deals, and contracts.
search_text: Account Company B2B HAS_COMPANY WORKS_AT
business_rules: Account = Company node (NOT a separate label)
cypher_template: MATCH (co:Company) RETURN count(co) AS account_count

name: Revenue / Order Volume
description: Total order value and count from CDP Order and CRM SalesOrder.
search_text: Revenue order volume total_amount PLACED SalesOrder
cypher_template: MATCH (o:Order) WHERE o.created_at >= datetime($period_start) AND o.created_at < datetime($period_end) RETURN count(o) AS order_count, sum(o.total_amount) AS revenue

name: Billing Cycle
description: Recurring invoicing interval inferred from Contract terms and Invoice issue dates.
search_text: Billing cycle invoice issue_date Contract ISSUED_TO FOR_COMPANY
cypher_template: MATCH (inv:Invoice)-[:ISSUED_TO]->(co:Company) WHERE inv.issue_date >= datetime($period_start) RETURN co.name AS company, count(inv) AS invoices, sum(inv.total) AS billed ORDER BY billed DESC LIMIT 10

name: Support Agent
description: Agent node linked to User via IS_AGENT_FOR; handles conversations via HANDLED_BY.
search_text: Support agent IS_AGENT_FOR HANDLED_BY conversation count
business_rules: ASSIGNED_TO is only for ContactProfile->User in CRM
cypher_template: MATCH (a:Agent)<-[:HANDLED_BY]-(c:Conversation) WHERE c.created_at >= datetime($period_start) RETURN a.display_name AS agent, count(c) AS handled ORDER BY handled DESC LIMIT 10

name: Period-over-Period Comparison
description: Compare a metric between current period and previous period; calculate absolute and percentage delta.
search_text: Period over period comparison increase decrease week over week delta diagnostic
business_rules: Always compute: current period count, previous period count, delta, pct_change
Prefer single aggregated query over multiple count queries
cypher_template: WITH $period_start AS ps, $period_end AS pe, $compare_start AS cs, $compare_end AS ce RETURN ps, pe, cs, ce
diagnostic_template: Use metric card cypher_template twice with CASE WHEN date in current vs previous period, or one query with conditional aggregation
examples: Why did X increase this week?
Compare this month vs last month

name: Top Contributors Breakdown
description: Rank dimensions (queue, channel, outcome, agent) by contribution to period-over-period delta.
search_text: Top contributors breakdown dimension delta root cause drivers
business_rules: Rank by abs(delta) not just current volume

name: Campaign Send Volume
description: Count of CampaignDelivery rows that were successfully sent (status=sent) for a campaign or channel in a period.
search_text: Campaign send volume messages sent delivery count CampaignDelivery status sent by channel
disambiguation: Use CampaignDelivery.status='sent' for delivered attempts. Do not count queued/pending. Audience size is audience_count / HAS_AUDIENCE_MEMBER, not sends.
business_rules: Filter by CampaignDelivery.created_at or opened/sent period with datetime($period_start)/datetime($period_end)
Break down by Channel via (CampaignDelivery)-[:THROUGH]->(Channel) using _channel or batch channel
Contact key is cdp_id; Campaign key is id; CampaignDelivery key is id
cypher_template: MATCH (d:CampaignDelivery)-[:FOR_CAMPAIGN]->(c:Campaign) WHERE d.status = 'sent' AND d.created_at >= datetime($period_start) AND d.created_at < datetime($period_end) RETURN count(d) AS sent_count
diagnostic_template: MATCH (d:CampaignDelivery)-[:THROUGH]->(ch:Channel) WHERE d.status='sent' WITH ch.name AS dimension, sum(CASE WHEN d.created_at >= datetime($period_start) AND d.created_at < datetime($period_end) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS current, sum(CASE WHEN d.created_at >= datetime($compare_start) AND d.created_at < datetime($compare_end) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS previous RETURN dimension, current, previous, current-previous AS delta ORDER BY abs(current-previous) DESC LIMIT 5
examples: How many messages were sent this week?

name: Campaign Open Rate
description: Share of sent CampaignDelivery rows that have at least one open (opened_at IS NOT NULL or open_count > 0).
search_text: Campaign open rate opened_at open_count CampaignDelivery engagement
disambiguation: Open rate uses CampaignDelivery engagement fields. Lifetime contact opens are on CampaignEngagement.email_open_count — different grain.
business_rules: Numerator: opened_at IS NOT NULL OR open_count > 0
Prefer channel=email for classic open rate; push/web may not track opens the same way
Filter organization_id and campaign id/name as needed
cypher_template: MATCH (d:CampaignDelivery) WHERE d.status='sent' AND d.created_at >= datetime($period_start) AND d.created_at < datetime($period_end) RETURN count(d) AS sent, sum(CASE WHEN d.opened_at IS NOT NULL OR d.open_count > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS opened, toFloat(sum(CASE WHEN d.opened_at IS NOT NULL OR d.open_count > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) / count(d) AS open_rate
examples: What is the open rate for the summer campaign?
Open rate by channel this month

name: Campaign Click Rate
description: Share of sent deliveries with at least one click (clicked_at IS NOT NULL or click_count > 0).
search_text: Campaign click rate CTR clicked_at click_count
disambiguation: Per-send CTR is on CampaignDelivery. Lifetime clicks are CampaignEngagement.email_click_count.
business_rules: Numerator clicked_at IS NOT NULL OR click_count > 0
Can also compute click-to-open: clicks / opens
cypher_template: MATCH (d:CampaignDelivery) WHERE d.status='sent' AND d.created_at >= datetime($period_start) AND d.created_at < datetime($period_end) RETURN count(d) AS sent, sum(CASE WHEN d.clicked_at IS NOT NULL OR d.click_count > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS clicked, toFloat(sum(CASE WHEN d.clicked_at IS NOT NULL OR d.click_count > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) / count(d) AS click_rate
examples: Which campaign has the best click rate?

name: Campaign Audience Size
description: Number of CDP Contacts included in a campaign audience at save/launch.
search_text: Campaign audience size HAS_AUDIENCE_MEMBER TARGETED_IN ReceivedCampaigns
disambiguation: audience_count on Campaign is the snapshot number. Exact members are (Campaign)-[:HAS_AUDIENCE_MEMBER]->(Contact) or TARGETED_IN ReceivedCampaigns. Send volume can be lower after suppressions/skips.
business_rules: Campaign.audience_count is denormalized snapshot — use for quick answers if graph edges incomplete
Draft audience uses DraftAudience-[:CONTAINS]->Contact before save
cypher_template: MATCH (c:Campaign)-[:HAS_AUDIENCE_MEMBER]->(ct:Contact) WHERE c.id = $campaign_id RETURN count(ct) AS audience_size
examples: How large is the audience for campaign X?
List contacts in the summer sale audience

name: Failed or Skipped Deliveries
description: CampaignDelivery rows with status failed or skipped; skip_fail_reason explains suppression, bounce, missing destination, etc.
search_text: Failed skipped deliveries skip_fail_reason suppression bounce
disambiguation: Skipped often means EmailSuppression or missing push endpoint. Failed means provider/ESP error. Not the same as unopened.
business_rules: Group by skip_fail_reason for root cause
Suppression soft-links EmailSuppression-[:BLOCKED]->CampaignDelivery when ETL emits it
cypher_template: MATCH (d:CampaignDelivery) WHERE d.status IN ['failed','skipped'] AND d.created_at >= datetime($period_start) AND d.created_at < datetime($period_end) RETURN d.status AS status, d.skip_fail_reason AS reason, count(*) AS cnt ORDER BY cnt DESC
diagnostic_template: MATCH (d:CampaignDelivery)-[:THROUGH]->(ch:Channel) WHERE d.status IN ['failed','skipped'] WITH ch.name AS dimension, sum(CASE WHEN d.created_at >= datetime($period_start) AND d.created_at < datetime($period_end) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS current, sum(CASE WHEN d.created_at >= datetime($compare_start) AND d.created_at < datetime($compare_end) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS previous RETURN dimension, current, previous, current-previous AS delta ORDER BY abs(current-previous) DESC LIMIT 5
examples: Failed deliveries by reason this week

name: Email Unsubscribe and Suppression
description: Contacts or emails that must not receive campaign email — CampaignEngagement.email_unsubscribed and/or EmailSuppression rows.
search_text: Unsubscribe suppression CampaignEngagement EmailSuppression opt out
disambiguation: CampaignEngagement is per Contact (cdp_id). EmailSuppression is per email string. Both block sends; suppression also covers hard_bounce and complaint.
cypher_template: MATCH (e:CampaignEngagement) WHERE e.email_unsubscribed = true RETURN count(e) AS unsubscribed_contacts

name: Email Channel Readiness
description: Whether the tenant email channel is ready to send — ChannelSendingProfile status=ready plus sender/domain/return-path/compliance/caps health.
search_text: Email channel readiness ChannelSendingProfile sender domain caps compliance
disambiguation: ChannelSendingProfile is the checklist gate. CampaignChannel.status=ready is per-campaign plan readiness, not tenant config.
business_rules: Tenant ready when ChannelSendingProfile for channel='email' has status='ready'
cypher_template: MATCH (p:ChannelSendingProfile)-[:THROUGH]->(ch:Channel) WHERE ch.name = 'email' OR p.channel = 'email' RETURN p.status AS profile_status

name: Campaigns Received by Contact
description: All campaigns targeted to or delivered to a CDP Contact via the ReceivedCampaigns hub.
search_text: ReceivedCampaigns hub contact campaign history HAS_RECEIVED_CAMPAIGNS
aliases: what campaigns did this contact get
disambiguation: Use Contact.cdp_id. Walk Contact-[:HAS_RECEIVED_CAMPAIGNS]->ReceivedCampaigns-[:CONTAINS]->CampaignDelivery-[:FOR_CAMPAIGN]->Campaign. Audience-only (not yet sent) uses MEMBER_OF_AUDIENCE / TARGETED_IN.
business_rules: Contact key property is cdp_id (NOT id)
Prefer deliveries for 'received/sent'; use HAS_AUDIENCE_MEMBER for 'targeted'
cypher_template: MATCH (ct:Contact {cdp_id: $cdp_id})-[:HAS_RECEIVED_CAMPAIGNS]->(hub:ReceivedCampaigns)-[:CONTAINS]->(d:CampaignDelivery)-[:FOR_CAMPAIGN]->(c:Campaign) RETURN c.name AS campaign, d.status AS status, d.opened_at AS opened_at, d.clicked_at AS clicked_at ORDER BY d.created_at DESC
examples: Which campaigns did contact X receive?
Show opens for this contact across campaigns

name: Anonymous vs Identified Visitor
description: WebsiteContacts mapped as Visitor. AnonymousVisitor when no CDP contact_id; IdentifiedVisitor when IDENTIFIED_AS Contact.
search_text: AnonymousVisitor IdentifiedVisitor website visitor IDENTIFIED_AS
disambiguation: Visitor is NOT Contact. Only promote/link via contact_id. Do not create a second Contact label from website_contacts.
business_rules: Web push may match PushEndpoint by endpoint URL (soft HAS_PUSH_SUBSCRIPTION)
cypher_template: MATCH (v:Visitor) RETURN sum(CASE WHEN v.contact_id IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS anonymous, sum(CASE WHEN v.contact_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS identified
examples: Which visitors were linked to contacts?

name: A/B Variant Performance
description: Compare open/click/sent metrics across CampaignDelivery.ab_variant values (a, b, holdout, winner).
search_text: A/B variant performance ab_variant holdout winner
disambiguation: ab_variant is on CampaignDelivery. Campaign.launch_plan JSON may also hold A/B config — prefer delivery rows for measured results.
business_rules: Only status='sent' in denominator for rates
holdout typically should not be messaged — verify status
cypher_template: MATCH (d:CampaignDelivery)-[:FOR_CAMPAIGN]->(c:Campaign) WHERE c.id = $campaign_id AND d.status='sent' RETURN d.ab_variant AS variant, count(d) AS sent, sum(CASE WHEN d.opened_at IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS opened, sum(CASE WHEN d.clicked_at IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS clicked
examples: Compare open rates for variant a vs b

name: Regulated Template Approval
description: Approval state of SMS/WhatsApp RegulatedTemplate required before regulated channel sends.
search_text: RegulatedTemplate WhatsApp DLT approval pending rejected
disambiguation: RegulatedTemplate is external-approval catalog. ChannelTemplate is the in-session creative draft. CampaignAlert ABOUT RegulatedTemplate for pending/rejected alerts.
business_rules: Link to campaign via FOR_CAMPAIGN when source_campaign_id set
cypher_template: MATCH (t:RegulatedTemplate) WHERE t.status = $status RETURN t.channel AS channel, t.name AS name, t.status AS status, t.rejected_reason AS rejected_reason ORDER BY t.updated_at DESC

name: Campaign Lifecycle
description: Campaign.status lifecycle: draft → scheduled/live → completed/cancelled. source_channel is origin (standalone_campaign|crm_marketing), not a Channel node.
search_text: Campaign lifecycle status draft live completed scheduled cancelled
disambiguation: Do not confuse source_channel with Channel stub (email/sms/...). Channel plans are CampaignChannel-[:THROUGH]->Channel.
cypher_template: MATCH (c:Campaign) RETURN c.status AS status, count(*) AS cnt ORDER BY cnt DESC

name: Campaign Channel Performance
description: Compare send/open/click/failure metrics across marketing channels for campaigns.
search_text: Campaign channel performance THROUGH Channel email sms whatsapp push
disambiguation: Always use shared Channel stub via THROUGH from CampaignChannel, CampaignSendBatch, or CampaignDelivery — do not invent a second channel node from campaign_channels.
business_rules: Batch also has channel property and THROUGH
cypher_template: MATCH (d:CampaignDelivery)-[:THROUGH]->(ch:Channel) WHERE d.created_at >= datetime($period_start) AND d.created_at < datetime($period_end) RETURN ch.name AS channel, count(d) AS deliveries, sum(CASE WHEN d.status='sent' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS sent, sum(CASE WHEN d.opened_at IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS opened ORDER BY sent DESC

name: Open Tickets
description: Tickets whose status is not terminal (still being worked). Prefer TicketStatus.is_terminal = false over hardcoding status names.
search_text: Open tickets active unresolved TicketStatus is_terminal false backlog DashboardMetrics
disambiguation: NOT Conversation volume (CCAAS). Use Ticket + TicketStatus. DashboardMetrics.open_tickets is a cached snapshot — prefer live Ticket count for accuracy.
business_rules: Always filter Ticket.organization_id for tenant scope
Filter created_at or updated_at with datetime($period_start) / datetime($period_end) when period asked
Optional fast path: (Tenant)-[:HAS_DASHBOARD_METRICS]->(DashboardMetrics) RETURN open_tickets (snapshot at captured_at)
cypher_template: MATCH (t:Ticket)-[:USES_STATUS]->(ts:TicketStatus) WHERE ts.is_terminal = false AND t.organization_id = $organization_id RETURN count(t) AS open_tickets
diagnostic_template: MATCH (t:Ticket)-[:USES_STATUS]->(ts:TicketStatus) WHERE ts.is_terminal = false AND t.organization_id = $organization_id WITH t.priority AS dimension, sum(CASE WHEN t.created_at >= datetime($period_start) AND t.created_at < datetime($period_end) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS current, sum(CASE WHEN t.created_at >= datetime($compare_start) AND t.created_at < datetime($compare_end) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS previous RETURN dimension, current, previous, current - previous AS delta ORDER BY abs(current - previous) DESC LIMIT 5
examples: How many open tickets do we have?
Why did open tickets increase this week?

name: Overdue Tickets
description: Non-terminal tickets whose resolution deadline (Ticket.due_at) is before now. due_at is computed from TicketSLA by priority at create/update.
search_text: Overdue tickets due_at past deadline TicketSLA GOVERNED_BY is_terminal false
disambiguation: Different from CCAAS SLAInstance.breached_at. Ticketing overdue uses Ticket.due_at on the Ticket node, optionally linked via GOVERNED_BY to TicketSLA.
business_rules: Overdue = due_at < datetime() AND status not terminal
Optional: (Ticket)-[:GOVERNED_BY]->(TicketSLA) for policy hours by priority
cypher_template: MATCH (t:Ticket)-[:USES_STATUS]->(ts:TicketStatus) WHERE ts.is_terminal = false AND t.due_at IS NOT NULL AND t.due_at < datetime() AND t.organization_id = $organization_id RETURN count(t) AS overdue_tickets
diagnostic_template: MATCH (t:Ticket)-[:USES_STATUS]->(ts:TicketStatus) WHERE ts.is_terminal = false AND t.due_at IS NOT NULL AND t.due_at < datetime() AND t.organization_id = $organization_id OPTIONAL MATCH (t)-[:IN_QUEUE]->(q:TicketQueue) RETURN coalesce(q.queue_name, 'Unqueued') AS dimension, count(t) AS overdue ORDER BY overdue DESC LIMIT 10
examples: Which queue has the most overdue tickets?

name: Unassigned Tickets
description: Open tickets with no L1 assignee (no ASSIGNED_TO TicketAgent, or assignee_id null).
search_text: Unassigned tickets no ASSIGNED_TO TicketAgent assignee_id null
disambiguation: ASSIGNED_TO on Ticket points to TicketAgent (ticketing), NOT CRM ContactProfile ASSIGNED_TO User, and NOT CCAAS Conversation HANDLED_BY Agent.
business_rules: Unassigned = NOT (Ticket)-[:ASSIGNED_TO]->(:TicketAgent) OR assignee_id IS NULL
cypher_template: MATCH (t:Ticket)-[:USES_STATUS]->(ts:TicketStatus) WHERE ts.is_terminal = false AND t.organization_id = $organization_id AND NOT (t)-[:ASSIGNED_TO]->(:TicketAgent) RETURN count(t) AS unassigned_tickets

name: Due Today Tickets
description: Open tickets whose due_at falls on the organization's local calendar today (OrgSettings.display_timezone).
search_text: Due today tickets due_at OrgSettings display_timezone DashboardMetrics
business_rules: Use Ticket.due_at date part in org timezone (OrgSettings.display_timezone)
cypher_template: MATCH (t:Ticket)-[:USES_STATUS]->(ts:TicketStatus) WHERE ts.is_terminal = false AND t.due_at IS NOT NULL AND date(t.due_at) = date() AND t.organization_id = $organization_id RETURN count(t) AS due_today
examples: How many tickets are due today?

name: Ticket Volume
description: Count of tickets created in a period; optionally breakdown by channel, priority, or TicketQueue.
search_text: Ticket volume created_at channel TicketQueue intake count period
disambiguation: NOT Conversation Volume (CCAAS). Ticketing work items are Ticket nodes.
business_rules: Filter by Ticket.created_at with datetime($period_start) / datetime($period_end)
cypher_template: MATCH (t:Ticket) WHERE t.organization_id = $organization_id AND t.created_at >= datetime($period_start) AND t.created_at < datetime($period_end) RETURN t.channel AS channel, count(t) AS volume ORDER BY volume DESC
diagnostic_template: MATCH (t:Ticket) WHERE t.organization_id = $organization_id WITH coalesce(t.channel, 'Unknown') AS dimension, sum(CASE WHEN t.created_at >= datetime($period_start) AND t.created_at < datetime($period_end) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS current, sum(CASE WHEN t.created_at >= datetime($compare_start) AND t.created_at < datetime($compare_end) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS previous RETURN dimension, current, previous, current - previous AS delta ORDER BY abs(current - previous) DESC LIMIT 5
examples: How many tickets were created this week?

name: Resolved Tickets
description: Tickets that reached a terminal status; prefer Ticket.resolved_at or TicketStatus.is_terminal = true.
search_text: Resolved tickets resolved_at is_terminal RESOLVED_BY TicketAgent
business_rules: Resolved when resolved_at IS NOT NULL OR (Ticket)-[:USES_STATUS]->(TicketStatus {is_terminal: true})
cypher_template: MATCH (t:Ticket) WHERE t.organization_id = $organization_id AND t.resolved_at >= datetime($period_start) AND t.resolved_at < datetime($period_end) RETURN count(t) AS resolved_tickets
examples: How many tickets resolved this week?

name: Ticket First Response Time
description: Time from ticket creation to first staff response (Ticket.first_response_at). SLA target hours come from TicketSLA.first_response_hours by priority.
search_text: First response time FRT first_response_at TicketSLA first_response_hours
disambiguation: CCAAS uses Conversation.first_agent_response_at / SLAInstance. Ticketing uses Ticket.first_response_at and TicketSLA.
business_rules: Only tickets with first_response_at IS NOT NULL
Met SLA if first_response_at <= created_at + TicketSLA.first_response_hours (via GOVERNED_BY)
cypher_template: MATCH (t:Ticket) WHERE t.organization_id = $organization_id AND t.first_response_at IS NOT NULL AND t.first_response_at >= datetime($period_start) AND t.first_response_at < datetime($period_end) RETURN avg(duration.between(t.created_at, t.first_response_at).seconds) AS avg_first_response_seconds
examples: What is average first response time?
Are we meeting first response SLA?

name: Ticket Resolution Time
description: Duration from Ticket.created_at to Ticket.resolved_at for resolved tickets.
search_text: Ticket resolution time created_at resolved_at TicketSLA resolution_hours
disambiguation: Not CCAAS Average Handle Time (assigned_at→resolved_at on Conversation). Ticketing ART uses created_at→resolved_at on Ticket.
business_rules: Only where resolved_at IS NOT NULL
cypher_template: MATCH (t:Ticket) WHERE t.organization_id = $organization_id AND t.resolved_at IS NOT NULL AND t.resolved_at >= datetime($period_start) AND t.resolved_at < datetime($period_end) RETURN avg(duration.between(t.created_at, t.resolved_at).seconds) AS avg_resolution_seconds

name: Ticket SLA Compliance
description: Share of resolved tickets that met resolution deadline (resolved_at <= due_at) or first-response deadline.
search_text: Ticket SLA compliance due_at resolved_at GOVERNED_BY TicketSLA breach met rate
disambiguation: CCAAS SLA breach uses SLAInstance.breached_at. Ticketing uses Ticket.due_at / first_response_at vs TicketSLA.
business_rules: Resolution SLA met: resolved_at IS NOT NULL AND due_at IS NOT NULL AND resolved_at <= due_at
Resolution breached: open with due_at < now, OR resolved_at > due_at
First-response met: first_response_at within TicketSLA.first_response_hours of created_at
cypher_template: MATCH (t:Ticket) WHERE t.organization_id = $organization_id AND t.resolved_at >= datetime($period_start) AND t.resolved_at < datetime($period_end) AND t.due_at IS NOT NULL WITH count(t) AS total, sum(CASE WHEN t.resolved_at <= t.due_at THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS met RETURN met, total, toFloat(met)/total AS sla_compliance_rate
examples: What is our ticket SLA compliance?
How many tickets breached SLA this week?

name: Ticket CSAT
description: Customer satisfaction on tickets: Ticket.csat_score (1–5) and csat_rated_at. Supports average, promoter/detractor rates, and response rate among resolved.
search_text: Ticket CSAT csat_score average satisfaction promoter detractor SupportProfile Contact
business_rules: Rated tickets: csat_score IS NOT NULL
Response rate = rated among resolved / resolved (resolved_at IS NOT NULL)
Do NOT invent a Customer node — Customer is Contact sublabel when contact_type = customer
cypher_template: MATCH (t:Ticket) WHERE t.organization_id = $organization_id AND t.csat_score IS NOT NULL AND t.csat_rated_at >= datetime($period_start) AND t.csat_rated_at < datetime($period_end) RETURN avg(toFloat(t.csat_score)) AS average_csat, count(t) AS rated_count
diagnostic_template: MATCH (t:Ticket)-[:REPORTED_VIA]->(sp:SupportProfile)-[:OVERLAY_OF]->(ct:Contact) WHERE t.organization_id = $organization_id AND t.csat_score IS NOT NULL AND t.csat_rated_at >= datetime($period_start) AND t.csat_rated_at < datetime($period_end) RETURN ct.cdp_id AS contact, avg(toFloat(t.csat_score)) AS avg_csat, count(t) AS ratings ORDER BY avg_csat ASC LIMIT 10
examples: What is average CSAT this month?

name: Ticket Escalation
description: Tickets escalated to an L2 resolver. Graph: Ticket has RESOLVED_BY TicketAgent and/or AuditEvent.action = ticket.escalated.
search_text: Ticket escalation RESOLVED_BY resolver AuditEvent ticket.escalated L2
disambiguation: Not CCAAS Transfer. Ticketing escalation sets resolver (RESOLVED_BY), distinct from L1 ASSIGNED_TO.
business_rules: Count distinct tickets in period via AuditEvent.created_at or when resolver_id set
cypher_template: MATCH (ae:AuditEvent)-[:ON_TICKET]->(t:Ticket) WHERE ae.organization_id = $organization_id AND ae.action = 'ticket.escalated' AND ae.created_at >= datetime($period_start) AND ae.created_at < datetime($period_end) RETURN count(DISTINCT t) AS escalation_volume

name: Ticket Queue Load
description: Workload on TicketQueue: open ticket count, assigned count, sla_status, and membership via HAS_MEMBER TicketAgent.
search_text: TicketQueue load open_tickets IN_QUEUE HAS_MEMBER MIRRORED_FROM Team
disambiguation: TicketQueue is ticketing (not CCAAS Queue). May be MIRRORED_FROM Team.
business_rules: Live load: count (Ticket)-[:IN_QUEUE]->(TicketQueue) with is_terminal = false
cypher_template: MATCH (q:TicketQueue) WHERE q.organization_id = $organization_id OPTIONAL MATCH (t:Ticket)-[:IN_QUEUE]->(q) OPTIONAL MATCH (t)-[:USES_STATUS]->(ts:TicketStatus) WITH q, sum(CASE WHEN ts.is_terminal = false THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS open_live RETURN q.queue_name AS queue, open_live, q.open_tickets AS open_cached, q.sla_status AS sla_status ORDER BY open_live DESC
examples: Which queue has the highest backlog?

name: Ticket Agent
description: TicketAgent is the ticketing workforce bridge to User (IS_TICKET_AGENT_FOR). Handles tickets via ASSIGNED_TO (L1) and RESOLVED_BY (L2).
search_text: TicketAgent IS_TICKET_AGENT_FOR User ASSIGNED_TO RESOLVED_BY not CCAAS Agent
disambiguation: NOT CCAAS Agent (IS_AGENT_FOR / HANDLED_BY Conversation). Ticket staff identity name/email/skills live on User; TicketAgent holds spoke prefs + setup_user_id.
business_rules: For display name use User via IS_TICKET_AGENT_FOR, not a name property on TicketAgent
cypher_template: MATCH (t:Ticket)-[:ASSIGNED_TO]->(ta:TicketAgent)-[:IS_TICKET_AGENT_FOR]->(u:User) WHERE t.organization_id = $organization_id AND t.created_at >= datetime($period_start) AND t.created_at < datetime($period_end) RETURN u.first_name + ' ' + u.last_name AS agent, count(t) AS assigned_count ORDER BY assigned_count DESC LIMIT 10
examples: Which agent has the most assigned tickets?

name: Support Requester
description: Person who reported a ticket. Path: Ticket-[:REPORTED_VIA]->SupportProfile-[:OVERLAY_OF]->Contact. Contact may also have Customer sublabel via contact_type.
search_text: Support requester REPORTED_VIA SupportProfile OVERLAY_OF Contact Customer sublabel ClientAccount
disambiguation: Do NOT create or MATCH a separate Customer node from ticketing. Use Contact (and optional :Customer sublabel). SupportProfile is spoke ops overlay (like CRM ContactProfile), keyed by contact_profile.id; person key is Contact.cdp_id.
business_rules: Customer KPIs (lifetime tickets, avg CSAT) aggregate Tickets under this path
SupportProfile.total_tickets is cache only — prefer count(Ticket) for analytics
cypher_template: MATCH (t:Ticket)-[:REPORTED_VIA]->(sp:SupportProfile)-[:OVERLAY_OF]->(ct:Contact) WHERE t.organization_id = $organization_id AND ct.cdp_id = $cdp_id RETURN count(t) AS tkt_total_tickets, avg(CASE WHEN t.csat_score IS NOT NULL THEN toFloat(t.csat_score) END) AS tkt_avg_csat_score
examples: How many tickets does this customer have?

name: High Priority Open Tickets
description: Open tickets with priority in urgent/high.
search_text: High priority open urgent tickets is_terminal false
cypher_template: MATCH (t:Ticket)-[:USES_STATUS]->(ts:TicketStatus) WHERE ts.is_terminal = false AND toLower(t.priority) IN ['urgent', 'high'] AND t.organization_id = $organization_id RETURN count(t) AS high_priority_open

name: Ticket Note Volume
description: Volume of TicketNote on tickets. visibility distinguishes internal vs customer-visible.
search_text: TicketNote volume visibility internal customer reply AUTHORED_BY
disambiguation: TicketNote is not CCAAS WorkNote on Conversation.
cypher_template: MATCH (n:TicketNote) WHERE n.organization_id = $organization_id AND n.created_at >= datetime($period_start) AND n.created_at < datetime($period_end) RETURN n.visibility AS visibility, count(n) AS note_volume
examples: How many ticket notes this week?

name: Outbound Ticket Email
description: Emails sent to customers about tickets (OutboundEmail). kinds include ticket_created, ticket_reply, ticket_resolved.
search_text: OutboundEmail SENT_FOR ticket_created ticket_reply ticket_resolved InboundEmailRef
business_rules: Filter OutboundEmail.created_at and status for delivery success
cypher_template: MATCH (e:OutboundEmail)-[:SENT_FOR]->(t:Ticket) WHERE e.organization_id = $organization_id AND e.created_at >= datetime($period_start) AND e.created_at < datetime($period_end) RETURN e.kind AS kind, count(e) AS email_volume
examples: How many outbound ticket emails this week?

name: Knowledge Article
description: Published help content as KnowledgeArticle. Distinct from accounts KnowledgeDocument.
search_text: KnowledgeArticle KB help center Published views not KnowledgeDocument
cypher_template: MATCH (a:KnowledgeArticle) WHERE a.organization_id = $organization_id AND a.status = 'Published' RETURN a.category AS category, count(a) AS articles, sum(a.views) AS total_views ORDER BY total_views DESC

name: Ticket Dashboard KPIs
description: Cached org KPI snapshot on DashboardMetrics: open_tickets, on_hold, overdue, due_today, unassigned. Use for quick home answers; live Ticket queries for authoritative analytics.
search_text: DashboardMetrics open overdue due_today unassigned home KPI snapshot
business_rules: One row per organization_id; check captured_at freshness
If snapshot stale or null, compute from Ticket + TicketStatus instead
cypher_template: MATCH (dm:DashboardMetrics) WHERE dm.organization_id = $organization_id RETURN dm.open_tickets AS open_tickets, dm.overdue AS overdue, dm.due_today AS due_today, dm.unassigned AS unassigned, dm.captured_at AS captured_at

name: Client Account Tickets
description: Tickets filed by contacts under a B2B ClientAccount (ticketing.ticketing_accounts). Not CRM Company and not MyAccount Tenant.
search_text: ClientAccount OF_ACCOUNT SupportProfile B2B tickets not Company Tenant
business_rules: Do not confuse ClientAccount with Company (CRM) or Tenant (accounts.organizations)
cypher_template: MATCH (t:Ticket)-[:REPORTED_VIA]->(sp:SupportProfile)-[:OF_ACCOUNT]->(ca:ClientAccount) WHERE ca.organization_id = $organization_id AND ca.name = $account_name RETURN count(t) AS ticket_count, avg(CASE WHEN t.csat_score IS NOT NULL THEN toFloat(t.csat_score) END) AS avg_csat
examples: How many tickets for account Acme?

name: Reopened Tickets
description: Tickets currently or historically in Reopened status (non-terminal). Indicates resolution quality issues.
search_text: Reopened tickets TicketStatus Reopened resolution quality
business_rules: Status key often 'Reopened' with is_terminal = false
Audit trail may show status transitions in AuditEvent.meta
cypher_template: MATCH (t:Ticket)-[:USES_STATUS]->(ts:TicketStatus) WHERE t.organization_id = $organization_id AND ts.status = 'Reopened' RETURN count(t) AS reopened_tickets

name: Ticket Automation Rule
description: Org AutomationRule that runs on ticket.created / ticket.updated to set priority, queue, assignee, or notify.
search_text: AutomationRule ticket.created ticket.updated auto assign queue
business_rules: conditions/actions are dynamic JSON on the node
cypher_template: MATCH (r:AutomationRule) WHERE r.organization_id = $organization_id AND r.enabled = true RETURN r.name AS rule, r.event AS event, r.priority AS run_order ORDER BY r.priority
